item.title: G Herbo Fraud Co-Defendant Avoids Prison After Hung Jury
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: G Herbo co-defendant Steven Hayes Jr. avoided prison after a hung jury and guilty plea in the stolen-card luxury spending case.
item.content:encoded:
G Herbo’s fraud co-defendant Steven Hayes Jr. avoided prison for his part in the stolen-card scheme that paid for jets, villas and designer puppies.

U.S. District Judge Mark G. Mastroianni sentenced Hayes, 34, to three years’ probation on October 8 in Springfield, Massachusetts. Prosecutors had sought four to six months in prison. The Justice Department announced the sentence October 14.

Hayes was held responsible for $44,814 in victim losses. The judge ordered him to pay $2,728 in restitution and forfeit the same amount.

The case went to trial in February, but jurors could not agree on a verdict. Hayes then pleaded guilty in May to conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Prosecutors charged six men in the case in 2020.

“Hayes and his co-conspirators used illicit account information to obtain, among other things, a private jet charter flight, a New York City villa rental, designer puppies from a pet boutique and car insurance. In total, Hayes was responsible for $44,814 in victim losses,” the Justice Department stated.

The purchases went through because the stolen card details belonged to real people. Once the card owners spotted charges they had not made, they disputed them. Card companies reversed the payments, leaving the businesses that supplied flights, lodging and goods with the losses.

G Herbo, whose legal name is Herbert Wright III, received his own probation sentence on January 11, 2024. He had pleaded guilty the previous July to wire fraud conspiracy and lying to a federal official.

His plea deal also led prosecutors to drop charges of aggravated identity theft.

The judge ordered the rapper to pay $139,968 in restitution and forfeiture, plus a $5,500 fine. His lawyers asked the judge to weigh his remorse, growth as a father and community work. They argued that he should stay out of prison.

Prosecutors said G Herbo used the fraud proceeds to travel to shows and post photos that promoted his career.

Those pictures showed him on private jets, in luxury cars and at a Jamaican villa. He also lied to a federal agent in November 2018, denying that he worked with or received help from promoter Antonio Strong.

Strong pleaded guilty in May 2024 and received nearly three years in prison that October. His scheme went beyond trips: prosecutors said he used fake names and claimed ties to music companies such as Sony and Universal to make fraudulent purchases.

Three other defendants, Joseph Williams, Demario Sorrells and celebrity barber Terrence Bender, also received probation.

Hayes’ sentence followed the earlier guilty pleas and punishments of all five of his co-defendants.

item.title: 50 Cent Questions More Shreveport Spending & Mayor Declines To Comment
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: 50 Cent said he's in no hurry for more Shreveport investment as the mayor declined to comment on his latest criticism.
item.content:encoded:
50 Cent said he’s in no hurry to put more money into Shreveport, while stressing that he still plans to do the work he already promised.

The rapper discussed his issues with the city on a new episode of “The Crew Has It,” hosted by Michael Rainey Jr. and Gianni Paolo, with Andrew Schulz also taking part. He said reviving a city without its support was a bad plan.

“The whole revitalization part of that idea…It’s just the idea of revitalizing a city without the city support is not a good idea,” 50 Cent said.

When KTBS sought a response on October 14, communications director Leigh Anne Evensky said the mayor had no comment on the rapper’s statements. She said the city would share news about future projects when appropriate.

“I’m not, not doing what I said I was going to do,” Fif clarified. “But I’m not in a hurry to invest and do the things outside beyond that because of the way they treated the situation.”

The conversation went beyond money. 50 Cent said he wanted officials to see him as a business owner. He also spoke about residents who had seen earlier promises go unfulfilled, saying that history helped explain their doubts about new plans.

His friction with City Hall predates the new interview.

AllHipHop reported in July that he had raised doubts about the separate Red River District proposal. Talks over that city-owned entertainment area beneath the Texas Street Bridge had slowed after inspections found major repairs were needed.

G-Unit wanted those repairs addressed before moving ahead.

The dispute grew when Arceneaux said on July 22 that representatives had been talking. AllHipHop’s July 23 report said 50 Cent checked with his lawyers and said they had received no communication from the city.

The larger studio plan already has state backing. Louisiana Economic Development announced on January 12 that G-Unit planned more than $124 million in work across three sites. The work includes upgrades at Stageworks and Millennium Studios, plus a dome-style venue and green space.

The state agreement offers up to $50 million for eligible infrastructure and modernization work. That support depends on performance, including local business involvement, economic impact and delivery of the improvements.

The city welcomed the plan in a January 13 statement saying it required no additional city funds. It had also signed the Stage Works lease with 50 Cent on June 6, 2025, for productions, events and multimedia work.

item.title: Shedeur Sanders Hires First NFL Agent: Young Money Sports’ CEO
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Shedeur Sanders hired Young Money APAA's Adie von Gontard as his first NFL agent, joining former teammate Travis Hunter.
item.content:encoded:
Shedeur Sanders hired his first NFL agent through Lil Wayne’s Young Money APAA Sports, joining the firm that already represents his former teammate Travis Hunter.

The Browns quarterback signed with Young Money APAA Sports founder and agency CEO Adie von Gontard.

ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the move Wednesday. Sanders had gone through the 2025 draft and the start of his pro career without a playing-contract agent.

The signing gave Lil Wayne’s sports business another client from the Colorado team coached by Deion Sanders.

Hunter joined Young Money for his NFL playing contracts before the 2025 draft, as AllHipHop reported at the time. Jacksonville later picked Hunter up with the second overall pick, and the agency still lists him among its NFL clients.

Lil Wayne co-founded the firm with the von Gontard family. Adie von Gontard started APAA Sports Group, which merged with Young Money in 2017. He is a certified NFL Players Association agent, and the firm’s work spans playing contracts, brand deals and equity stakes in businesses.

Sanders already had a team to help him make money off the field.

He and Hunter worked with SMAC Entertainment before the draft. SMAC helped them land paid brand deals while they were still in college, Front Office Sports reported in April 2025.

Those college deals let both players earn money from the use of their names, images and likenesses. Both still used SMAC for off-field work as they prepared to turn pro. But Hunter had picked Young Money to handle his playing contracts, while Sanders still had no NFL agent.

Their ties ran beyond the field. Before the draft, SMAC CEO Constance Schwartz-Morini told Front Office Sports, “This is a real friendship and family dynamic that won’t end when their time at Colorado’s up.”

Cleveland selected Sanders in the fifth round with the 144th pick in 2025 and announced his rookie signing on May 19 that year. He started seven games in his first season, throwing for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

He has served as Deshaun Watson’s backup this season. Through the Browns’ first five games, the team’s official stats listed Sanders with one pass attempt and no starts.

item.title: Wale Joins CapSole As Co-Owner & Creative Chief
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Wale's CapSole deal puts the sneaker collector in charge of creative direction as the brand builds its preservation business.
item.content:encoded:
Wale took an ownership stake in CapSole and became its chief creative officer, bringing his sneaker obsession into the preservation business.

Footwear News revealed the Washington, D.C., rapper’s new role on Wednesday, October 14. CapSole’s website now lists him as an owner and CCO, placing him at a company that sells sneaker preservation kits.

His work will cover the brand’s creative direction, cultural partnerships and growth. Wale told FN he wanted a stake in the company and a voice in how it develops. He said he believed in founder Darren Lee’s work and wanted to help build it.

For Lee, bringing the rapper aboard connects the products to the meaning people attach to their collections.

“It’s about preserving the stories, culture and memories attached to them,” Lee said.

Lee started CapSole in 2019 after looking for a way to keep his own sneakers from breaking down. The company says it worked with chemical engineers and preservation specialists to develop its system, aiming to protect shoes that hold both personal and financial value for collectors.

Its kits pair a reusable, airtight pod with a preservative.

The brand markets the system for use between wears, so owners can take their sneakers out and then seal them away again. Its website also ties the business to a broader mission of teaching collectors about preservation and sustainability.

That focus fits a long-running part of Wale’s life. In a GQ interview, he explained why Air Jordan 3s held a place among his essentials.

“I’ve always been a Nike person. The shoes represent so much more to me,” he said.

His ties to footwear have since moved beyond his own closet. In 2025, Wale and basketball prospect AJ Dybantsa first debuted Nike’s G.T. Future during NBA All-Star Weekend. Nike used the new model to pair performance basketball technology with a futuristic look, making Wale the face of its introduction to sneaker fans.

He has also brought that culture into his music and retail partnerships. In 2022, he teamed with NTWRK on a raffle for retro Tiffany Nike SB Dunks tied to his “Tiffany Nikes” video. The rollout included a limited-edition sneaker pillow that linked the song to collectible merchandise.

The deal’s financial terms and the size of Wale’s ownership stake have not been disclosed.

item.title: Da Baby & Fetty Wap Join SpinKing In The Visual For “Beat Go”
item.dc:creator: Brxton Lee
item.description: DJ SpinKing teams up with DaBaby and Fetty Wap for the high-energy “Beat Go” music video, delivering a club-ready anthem produced alongside Grammy-winning hitmaker Boi-1da.
item.content:encoded:
DJ SpinKing keeps the party going with the release of Ty Tiomico-directed visual for “Beat Go” featuring fellow Jersey native Fetty Wap and Carolina chart-topper DaBaby. Featuring the instrumentation of multi-platinum, Grammy-winning producer Boi-1da, this high-definition clip perfectly captures the song’s infectious rhythm, tailor-made for dance floors, live sets, and viral social moments.

Co-produced by SpinKing, whose ability to bring together major artists and create records built for movement is at the center of the track, the high-energy, club-focused record effortlessly turns any moment into an epic experience.

Watch the music video for “Beat Go” via DNR Music Group / Asylum Records (Warner Music Group) after the jump! 

M

STREAM via DSPs

https://djspinking.lnk.to/BeatGo

Short Biography

Born in the Bronx but raised in New Jersey, SpinKing began his DJ career at the age of 17. He made his mixtape debut in 2011 with Hip House featuring Meek Mill and Fatman Scoop. Hip House 2 followed in 2013 and featured the single “Body Operator,” along with appearances from French Montana and Jeremih. He signed with the eOne that same year, then in 2014, he partnered with producer Vinylz for the single “Adult Swim” featuring A$AP Ferg and Tyga. Following the success of Hip House 2, DJ SpinKing released his latest mixtape, For The Culture, which features 50 Cent, Torey Lanez, Ty Dolla $ign and more. 

To date, SpinKing has produced records for PNB Rock, Young Jeezy and more. Climbing the charts, in 2017 “Timeless” with A Boogie, went platinum with over 1 million units sold! In 2018, DJ SpinKing released “TATI” with Tekashi 6ix9nine, which landed 6ix9ine his seventh entry on the Billboard Hot 100 Charts. DJ SpinKing shows no sign of slowing down, officially launching his record label, DNR Music Group, a joint venture with Asylum Records and Warner Music Group.

item.title: Feds Leave Kanye West Interview Counts Out Of Reworked Journalist Case
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Kanye West's leaked interview was left out of specific charges as prosecutors rebuilt their case against journalist Timothy Burke.
item.content:encoded:
Federal prosecutors rebuilt their case against journalist Timothy Burke, but left out the specific charges tied to Kanye West’s leaked Tucker Carlson interview.

The dispute grew out of footage that exposed remarks Fox News left out of Kanye’s interview. Motherboard published clips containing antisemitic remarks and conspiracy theories, which drew attention to what viewers had not heard in the broadcast.

A grand jury returned a new indictment October 8. Burke faced 13 charges, down from 14 in the original case. Prosecutors still accused him of a wider scheme to take material from computer systems without permission.

The earlier case accused Burke of capturing the October 6, 2022 interview and sharing clips four days later.

The new indictment dropped those entries. The only charge that still accused him of sharing footage concerned a separate clip in which a host discussed a hurricane’s possible effect on his home.

The new case included conspiracy, six computer-access charges and six charges under the federal Wiretap Act.

The new version described other behind-the-scenes conversations, including a weather correspondent and camera crew preparing to cover an approaching hurricane.

The filing followed a major setback for the government. U.S. District Judge Kathryn Kimball Mizelle threw out seven Wiretap Act counts in September 2025 because prosecutors had left out facts they needed to allege and prove.

Her ruling required the government to show that Burke was not a party to the communications and that the electronic streams were not readily available to the public.

The rewritten charges added that language.

“Significant First Amendment concerns arise if I were to adopt the government’s theory. To cure this constitutional concern, I look to the statutory exceptions and conclude that the government must plead and prove two of them: that a defendant was not a ‘party to the communication’ and that any electronic communication was not ‘readily accessible to the general public,'” Mizelle wrote in the earlier ruling.

The judge allowed prosecutors to bring corrected charges. They first pursued an appeal, then abandoned that effort last month before obtaining the new indictment.

Burke’s defense has maintained that he gathered news from publicly accessible material.

The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press supported his challenge, warning that the government’s approach could threaten legitimate reporting.

“Burke does not dispute that he acquired the communications, but instead whether he did so consistent with the Wiretap Act exceptions. The government’s arguments (and I assume evidence) are that he did not. So although this order shifts the burden of proof on those exceptions, it does not alter the focus of the trial,” Mizelle wrote.

Burke also sought to end the prosecution over delays, citing his right to a speedy trial. His next reply in that fight was due October 16.

item.title: Snoop Dogg’s Costa Rica Show Canceled After Promoter’s Arrest Over Drug Operation
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Snoop Dogg's Costa Rica concert was canceled days after a reassurance from its promoter, who remained under investigation.
item.content:encoded:
Snoop Dogg‘s Costa Rica concert was canceled just days after the man behind it told fans it would go ahead, despite his arrest in a money-laundering case.

Stockwell Entretenimiento said the December 3 show at the Pedregal event center in Belén was off. The company said it reached a mutual agreement with Snoop and promised automatic refunds, but gave no reason for the cancellation or a date for fans to get their money back.

Just four days earlier, the same team had stood by the date and said it was still working on the show. Tickets had been sold through Publitickets.

The company’s owner, Don Stockwell, was arrested on October 7 and released the next morning in the Éxodo case. He has denied wrongdoing and remained under investigation following his release.

Police said they were looking at claims that a group used cash from drug sales to fund past concerts. Michael Soto, an official with the country’s Judicial Investigation Agency, said the artists who played those shows had no link to the case.

Soto said roughly $859,000 flowed into three events tied to Stockwell and fellow producer Hugo Barboza. Police were trying to learn whether the shows were used to make cash from alleged drug sales look like lawful earnings.

Police linked the money to a group they said was led by Edwin Vargas García, known as “Sobrino.” Soto said the events took place in 2024 and 2025, before Snoop’s planned December show.

Stockwell’s lawyer, Daniel Brenes, said his client worked with Barboza, who found people to fund shows. He said Stockwell did not know the man introduced to him as Edwin had been arrested in a drug case.

Meanwhile, Brenes told CRHoy that the prosecutor handling the case told him he planned to ask to have Stockwell held in jail. The hearing was still underway when Brenes spoke, and he said the request had not yet been made.

“Ticket refunds will be processed automatically, and in accordance with current Costa Rican law,” the company said in its Spanish-language statement.

Stockwell Entretenimiento did not announce a replacement date for Snoop’s performance.

item.title: D’Angelo Remembered One Year After Death, Nashville Museum Unveils Tribute Film
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: D’Angelo receives a heartfelt Nashville homage as treasured archival portraits and an intimate remembrance emerges from private custody.
item.content:encoded:
D’Angelo‘s musical legacy tooks center stage again as the National Museum of African American Music (NMAAM) marked the first anniversary of his death with a public film premiere and a day devoted to his extraordinary influence.

The museum, located in Nashville, organized a special commemoration honoring Michael Archer, the acclaimed singer and musician known worldwide as D’Angelo, with activities both online and at its Nashville location.

The centerpiece was the public premiere of ANOTHER LIFE: The Enduring Art of Michael Archer, a 14-minute documentary co-directed by Brennan “Will Coloan” Williams and D’Angelo’s cousin Lisa R. Mabry Pulley.

Music industry maven Dyana Williams, close friend of the late singer and co-founder of Black Music Month, said D’Angelo resonates on many levels as a person and artist.

“D’Angelo respected the superlative creativity of the founding ancestors he deeply admired in multiple genres,” she told AllHipHop. “On this first year anniversary of his transition, we are paying homage to this innovative, once in a lifetime artist, composer, father, brother, family member, friend and beloved appreciated by millions worldwide.”

READ ALSO: Media Maven Dyana Williams On Black Music, & Why “Business Music” Is Still Exploits The Culture…

Previously screened exclusively at the singer’s private memorial last year, the film is now being presented to the public for the first time.

The production features previously unseen family photographs chronicling Archer’s life from his beginnings in Richmond, Virginia, to his emergence as an internationally celebrated musician.

For those who knew D’Angelo primarily through his recordings and performances, the documentary offers a more intimate perspective on the man behind the music.

Veteran journalist Tonya Pendleton, who interviewed D’Angelo for XXL magazine in the late 1990s, reflected on the extraordinary talent and artistic integrity that distinguished the singer from his contemporaries.

“The loss of D’Angelo continues to resonate even a year later. He was one of the brightest stars in the soul/R&B firmament and it feels so harsh to have him taken from us so before his time.”

Pendleton also stressed that his three studio albums remain essential documents of his musical brilliance.

The museum’s tribute extends beyond the film to examine the musical traditions that helped shape his artistry.

Visitors can experience Remember The Sound: On the Feeling of D’Angelo, an audio documentary by Dr. Wesley J. Watkins IV that explores the historical foundations of his sound.

The presentation traces musical connections from West and Central West Africa to Congo Square before examining the influence of gospel, blues, funk and producer J Dilla.

That historical perspective places D’Angelo’s work within a much larger musical lineage and examines the traditions that informed his contributions to contemporary Black music.

Th museum’s Amplify store is hosting the documentary presentations alongside personal items from D’Angelo’s life and his Homegoing program.

Families can also participate in a scavenger hunt through the museum’s galleries.

NMAAM Radio is dedicating its programming to the singer’s catalog, accompanied by messages from musicians who worked with him and people who knew him personally.

The broadcasts are available through the museum’s website and its iOS radio application, allowing listeners outside Nashville to participate in the anniversary observance.

The commemoration concludes at 7 p.m. with NMAAM & Orchestra Noir Present: The Culture 2000 Tour II, An Inside Look, a free evening featuring conversation and live musical performances.

The museum also thanked the Archer family and founding board member Dyana Williams for their contributions to the tribute.

For Pendleton, the anniversary is also a painful reminder of the music the world will never hear and the creative possibilities that died with him.

She said, “We can only mourn what he could have contributed, but that and his musically talented children are what we have to remember him by. He represented something truly special – an artist intentional about his music and one who cared more about it than just about anyone else.”

D’Angelo’s legacy remains both a remarkable body of work and an unfinished musical journey with NMAAM celebrating his life in ways previously unseen. 

“May his cultural impact be felt forever,” Dyana Williams said in closing.

item.title: “Hamilton” Reaches 500 No. 1 Weeks On Billboard’s Cast Albums Chart
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Hamilton reached 500 weeks atop Billboard's Cast Albums chart, extending a run shaped by Lin-Manuel Miranda and The Roots.
item.content:encoded:
Lin-Manuel Miranda‘s Hamilton reached its 500th week at No. 1 on Billboard’s Cast Albums chart, giving the Hip-Hop musical a record that stretched far beyond Broadway.

The original Broadway cast recording reached the milestone on the October 17 chart. Billboard said no other title had spent 500 weeks at No. 1 on any of its currently published rankings.

That run covered most of the album’s 11 years on the list. It led for 500 of its 576 chart weeks, or about 87% of the time. “Wicked” ranked next among cast albums with 355 weeks on top.

Members of The Roots helped shape the album’s sound. Questlove and Black Thought joined the production team as Miranda turned Alexander Hamilton’s life into a story told through rap, R&B and show tunes.

Their role went beyond lending famous names to the credits. Music director Alex Lacamoire recalled their input in a 2016 Berklee interview. The Roots pushed the team to make the studio recording sound different from the stage show.

They urged the producers to bring drums and scratches forward, distort a hi-hat and try delay on a vocal. Those choices gave the album room to work as a rap record in its own right, rather than simply capture a night in the theater.

“Those guys were able to push us in a direction we might not have gone,” Lacamoire said.

He also credited mixer Tim Latham, who had worked with A Tribe Called Quest, De La Soul, Erykah Badu and D’Angelo. That background helped Latham balance rap and theater.

Lacamoire wanted live players to recreate sounds often made on computers, keeping the feel of a band within the score.

The show later reached viewers at home who could experience the original cast.

Disney+ released the filmed stage production in July 2020, using performances captured at the Richard Rodgers Theatre in June 2016. Miranda played Hamilton opposite Leslie Odom Jr.’s Aaron Burr, with Daveed Diggs taking on Lafayette and Thomas Jefferson.

That streaming debut also helped the cast recording reach a Billboard 200 peak of No. 2 in July 2020. The album has now logged 575 weeks on that all-genre chart.

item.title: Ludacris Uses Disguises & Hotel Workouts To Stay Fit On Tour
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ludacris revealed how disguises and hotel-room workouts helped him keep up his fitness routine while traveling for shows.
item.content:encoded:
Ludacris sometimes put on a disguise just to take a walk while touring. It lets him get outside without being recognized.

The rapper explained in a new interview that long stretches in cars, on planes and in hotel rooms made fresh air a priority. His road routine also included Zoom workouts in his hotel room when his trainer couldn’t join him.

“Even if I am somehow kind of blending in and hiding in plain sight, just being able to breathe fresh air is very important to me since I’m trapped in so many planes, cars and hotels without balconies,” Ludacris said.

Luda described training five to seven days a week, using hotel gyms when possible. Without one, he turned to outdoor bodyweight exercises or brought free weights into his room. Back home in Atlanta, he had converted a garage into a gym.

That effort began with a deeply personal moment. In 2023, he told Men’s Health that losing his father to alcoholism pushed him to take better care of himself. His dad died at 52, when Ludacris was 29.

He tied his goals to time with his children and future grandchildren, and to staying strong enough to give fans a full show for years to come. His training also included martial arts and the street-fighting style known as 52 Blocks.

“I am noticing [my] age, but I’m up for the challenge. I’m a warrior,” he said.

The planning went beyond finding somewhere to lift weights. In 2024, he told Us Weekly that he mapped out meals ahead of time so hunger wouldn’t make him grab whatever was nearby.

“You got to plan out the workouts and plan out the meals,” he said.

He described working different muscle groups on different days and making room for rest. On days off, he relaxed, recovered and allowed himself a cheat day, rather than treating every day as another hard session.

His latest comments came amid his partnership with One A Day. The brand’s “Health Doesn’t Need to Be Ludacris” campaign, launched earlier this year, played on his name to mock elaborate wellness fads and promote a simpler routine.

For all the work he put into fitting exercise around travel, Ludacris placed one daily habit first.

“Get enough sleep…that’s the number one priority,” he said.
